==English==

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/tiːt͡ʃ/|[tʰɪi̯t͡ʃ]}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-teach.wav|a=Southern England}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-teach.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|iːtʃ|s=1}}
* {{hyph|en|teach}}

===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*deyḱ-}}
{{ety|en|id=instruct|:inh|enm:techen|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|techen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|tǣċan|t=to show, declare, demonstrate; teach, instruct, train; assign, prescribe, direct; warn; persuade}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*taikijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*taikijaną|t=to show}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*deyḱ-|t=to show}}.

Cognate with {{cog|sco|tech}}, {{m|sco|teich|t=to teach}}, {{cog|de|zeigen|t=to show, point out}}, {{m|de|zeihen|t=accuse, blame}}, {{cog|got|𐌲𐌰𐍄𐌴𐌹𐌷𐌰𐌽|t=to announce, declare, tell, show, display}}, {{cog|la|dīcō|t=speak, say, tell}}, {{cog|grc|δείκνυμι|t=show, point out, explain, teach}}, {{cog|sa|दिशति|t=to point out, show, tell, teach}}. More at {{l|en|token}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb|~es|~ing|taught}}

# {{lb|en|ditransitive}} To [[pass]] on [[knowledge]] to.
#: {{syn|en|educate|instruct}}
#: {{ux|en|Can you '''teach''' me to sew?  Can you '''teach''' sewing to me?}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|stative}} To [[pass]] on [[knowledge]] generally, especially as one's profession; to act as a [[teacher]].
#: {{ant|en|learn}}
#: {{ux|en|She used to '''teach''' at university.}}
# {{lb|en|ditransitive}} To [[cause]] (someone) to [[learn]] or [[understand]] (something).
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=8|passage=The humor of my proposition appealed more strongly to Miss Trevor than I had looked for, and from that time forward she became her old self again;{{nb...}}. Now she had come to look upon the matter in its true proportions, and her anticipation of a possible chance of '''teaching''' him a lesson was a pleasure to behold.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2013|month=September-October|author=[http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/robert-l-dorit Rob Dorit]
|magazine=w:American Scientist|title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/pub/2013/5/making-life-from-scratch Making Life from Scratch]
|passage=Deep Blue '''taught''' us a great deal about the power of the human mind precisely because it could not reproduce the intuitive and logical leaps of Kasparov’s mind. A truly synthetic cell, built from scratch or even from preexisting components, will be a cell without ancestry, and it, too, will '''teach''' us a great deal about the underlying complexities of life without actually reproducing them.}}
# {{lb|en|ditransitive}} To [[cause]] to [[know]] the [[disagreeable]] [[consequences]] of some action.
#: {{ux|en|I'll '''teach''' you to make fun of me!}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete|transitive}} To show (someone) the way; to [[guide]], [[conduct]]; to [[point]], [[indicate]].
#: {{ux|en|‘The bliss is there’, mumbled the old man and '''taught''' to Heaven.}}
#* {{RQ:Mlry MrtDrthr|8.5|2|VI|v|passage=So thus within a whyle as they thus talked the nyghte passed / and the daye shone / and thenne syre launcelot armed hym / and took his hors / and they '''taught''' hym to the Abbaye and thyder he rode within the space of two owrys}}
<!--Prior quote:Than Sir Launcelot armed hym and toke his horse, and so he was '''taughte''' to the abbey.-->
